items.headline: Extreme Greed returns while valuation remains extreme
items.summary: The live AGCI engine moved to Greed 80/100 (Extreme Greed), up 2 points daily, while Valuation remains 87/100. The matrix escalated to EUPHORIA_RISK / Capital preservation / Do not chase.
items.whyItMatters: Complacency is now extreme while aggregate valuation still offers little margin of safety. Preserve liquidity and avoid chasing broad beta despite recent equity resilience.

items.headline: Anthropic IPO debate intensifies as competition and safety collide
items.summary: Barron's new magazine edition centers on whether public markets are prepared for a potential Anthropic IPO. Reuters reports Anthropic is considering another model release amid competitive pressure while the industry faces a broader safety and governance reckoning.
items.whyItMatters: A major frontier-model IPO could create a new public-market valuation benchmark for AI, but safety, governance, competitive durability, customer concentration and financing quality must be underwritten alongside revenue growth. Do not treat prospective IPO demand as proof of sustainable economics.

items.headline: Saudi workaround supports Asian crude flows while European disruption persists
items.summary: Saudi Aramco is preparing roughly 60 million barrels of Gulf exports for September and October using ship-to-ship transfers near Sohar, helping offset lost Yanbu flows. At the same time, some October deliveries to European refiners have been halted after damage to the East-West pipeline.
items.whyItMatters: The workaround reduces immediate global scarcity risk but redistributes rather than eliminates physical bottlenecks. Maintain a moderate energy hedge without chasing crude; monitor freight, diesel, European refining and pipeline restoration.

items.headline: Mexico and US report progress toward a trade agreement
items.summary: President Claudia Sheinbaum said Mexico is working toward a trade agreement with the United States after a call with President Trump. Negotiations are progressing, but no final terms have been disclosed; Mexico continues seeking relief on steel, aluminum and auto tariffs.
items.whyItMatters: This is a positive negotiating signal for nearshoring and Mexican industrial assets, but it is not yet an investable policy outcome. Maintain selective exposure and wait for binding terms on tariffs, autos, rules of origin and Chinese investment.

items.headline: Renewed Saudi security risk complicates the oil normalization narrative
items.summary: Saudi authorities issued rare aerial-threat warnings around Riyadh and Al-Kharj, and smoke and flames were observed near Riyadh's main airport after overnight booms. Attribution of the specific incident was not confirmed in the initial report.
items.whyItMatters: Even as crude logistics improve, direct security risk to Saudi infrastructure remains elevated. Do not equate lower oil prices with geopolitical normalization; retain flexible Gulf travel plans and energy-risk protection.
